name: es30-post-processing
title: Post-processing: gamma, blur, Sobel, bloom, depth of field
summary: An animated, lit 3D scene (orbiting camera, checker floor, torus, spheres, cubes, two orbiting point lights, fog) is rendered into offscreen framebuffers (RGBA8 color texture + depth texture; SRGB8_ALPHA8 texture + depth renderbuffer) and post-processed with full-screen passes that read their input with texelFetch: sRGB gamma in the shader and with an SRGB8_ALPHA8 scene target, separable Gaussian blur with ping-pong targets, Sobel edges, bloom (bright-pass + blur + add) and depth of field from the depth texture. Every pass is recomputed on the CPU from the bytes the GPU read back and compared over all pixels; scene pixels (sky, floor lighting, lamp bulbs, floor depth) are checked analytically; six negative controls show that the checks can fail.
spec: ES 3.0 §4.4.1 Binding and Managing Framebuffer Objects, §4.4.2.1 Renderbuffer Objects, §4.4.2.3 / §4.4.2.4 Attaching Renderbuffer / Texture Images, §4.4.4 Framebuffer Completeness, §4.4.3 Feedback Loops Between Textures and the Framebuffer (the pass structure avoids them)

ES 3.0 §3.8.13 Texture Completeness (NEAREST filters), §3.8.15.1 Depth Texture Comparison Mode (mode NONE returns the stored depth), §2.12.9.2 Texel Fetches (point sampling, no wrap mode, out-of-range coordinates undefined)
ES 3.0 §3.8.16 sRGB Texture Color Conversion (equation 3.26), §4.1.8 sRGB Conversion (equation 4.1), §6.1.13 Framebuffer Object Queries (FRAMEBUFFER_ATTACHMENT_COLOR_ENCODING)
ES 3.0 §2.1.6 Fixed-Point Data Conversions (equations 2.1, 2.3: the 8-bit quantization between passes), §2.1.1 Floating-Point Computation, §4.1.9 Dithering (disabled)

ES 3.0 §2.13.1 Controlling the Viewport (window-space depth), §3.6.1 Basic Polygon Rasterization (perspective-correct interpolation, face culling), §4.1.5 Depth Buffer Test, §4.2.3 Clearing the Buffers, §4.3.2 Reading Pixels

GLSL ES 3.00 §8.8 Texture Lookup Functions (texelFetch, textureSize), §8.9 Fragment Processing Functions (fwidth), §4.5.4 Default Precision Qualifiers (lowp sampler2D by default; the lookup result has the precision of the sampler, section 12 Issues), §7.1 / §7.2 Special Variables (gl_VertexID, gl_FragCoord), §8.2 Exponential Functions, §8.3 Common Functions, §6.3 Iteration

api.glGenTextures: RGBA8 / SRGB8_ALPHA8 scene and pass targets and a DEPTH_COMPONENT24 depth texture; every pass reads them and matches the CPU model
api.glBindTexture: TEXTURE_2D bound to the units of each pass; the sampled images match the CPU model
api.glActiveTexture: units 0 to 5 hold the six inputs of the present pass; each look reads the right image
api.glTexImage2D: RGBA8, SRGB8_ALPHA8 (RGBA/UNSIGNED_BYTE) and DEPTH_COMPONENT24 (DEPTH_COMPONENT/UNSIGNED_INT) storage without data; contents read back with glReadPixels or through the depth-dump pass
api.glTexParameteri: NEAREST min/mag and CLAMP_TO_EDGE (typed glTexParameter overloads) make every target texture complete; an incomplete texture would sample as black and fail every pass comparison (indirect verification)
api.glGenRenderbuffers: DEPTH_COMPONENT24 renderbuffer of the SRGB8_ALPHA8 scene
api.glRenderbufferStorage: depth renderbuffer storage; the SRGB8_ALPHA8 scene, drawn with its depth test, equals the encoded RGBA8 scene at every pixel
api.glGenFramebuffers: scene, bright-pass, ping, blur, bloom and edge framebuffers
api.glBindFramebuffer: FRAMEBUFFER for every pass, READ_FRAMEBUFFER for readback; the default framebuffer shows the presented image
api.glFramebufferTexture2D: COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 textures (RGBA8, SRGB8_ALPHA8) and a DEPTH_ATTACHMENT depth texture; render-to-texture results compared pixel by pixel
api.glFramebufferRenderbuffer: DEPTH_ATTACHMENT renderbuffer on the SRGB8_ALPHA8 scene framebuffer
api.glCheckFramebufferStatus: FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE required for every framebuffer configuration (color only, color + depth texture, color + depth renderbuffer; init throws otherwise)
api.glGetFramebufferAttachmentParameteriv: FRAMEBUFFER_ATTACHMENT_COLOR_ENCODING is GL_SRGB for the SRGB8_ALPHA8 scene texture and GL_LINEAR for the RGBA8 one; the default framebuffer's encoding is queried to decide whether present.frag must undo a second encoding
api.glReadPixels: RGBA/UNSIGNED_BYTE readback of every offscreen target (stored bytes for SRGB8_ALPHA8) and of the default framebuffer, compared with the CPU model
api.glGenVertexArrays: one VAO per mesh plus an attribute-less VAO for the full-screen triangle
api.glBindVertexArray: mesh VAOs (element array buffer is VAO state) and the empty VAO for passes
api.glGenBuffers: vertex and index buffers of the four meshes
api.glBufferData: interleaved position + normal data and 16-bit indices; the rendered floor and lamp pixels match the CPU projection and lighting
api.glEnableVertexAttribArray: position and normal attributes of the scene program
api.glVertexAttribPointer: stride 24 bytes, offsets 0 and 12; lit floor pixels depend on correct normals
api.glDrawElements: UNSIGNED_SHORT indexed triangles of floor, torus, spheres and cubes; floor pixels, lamp bulbs and depth match the CPU reference
api.glDrawArrays: TRIANGLES, 3 vertices from gl_VertexID: the full-screen triangle of every pass covers every pixel exactly once
api.glUseProgram: sky, scene, bright, blur, sobel, depth-dump and present programs
api.glGetUniformLocation: uniforms of all seven programs located (the passes would not match otherwise)
api.glUniform1i: sampler units, u_kind, u_mode, u_radius, u_fb_srgb
api.glUniform1f: threshold, edge thresholds, bloom strength, depth range, focus parameters, fog constant, material parameters
api.glUniform2f: u_resolution of the sky pass (sky gradient equals the CPU model)
api.glUniform2i: u_dir (1,0) / (0,1) of the blur passes; both directions match the CPU Gaussian
api.glUniform3f: colors, eye, directional light and camera basis; floor lighting and sky equal the CPU model
api.glUniform3fv: two point-light positions and colors (arrays); the floor lighting depends on both
api.glUniformMatrix4fv: view-projection and model matrices; CPU-projected lamp centers hit the bulb pixels, floor depth matches the analytic value
api.glViewport: full-target viewport of every pass: pixel (x, y) of a pass reads texel (x, y)
api.glClear: COLOR | DEPTH of the scene targets; the depth part is observed (sky pixels keep the cleared depth 1.0, read through the depth-dump pass); the color part is overdrawn by the sky pass and not observed
api.glClearDepthf: depth cleared to 1.0, observed at sky pixels
api.glEnable: DEPTH_TEST for the lit geometry: the floor's depth is stored (matches the analytic window depth)
api.glDisable: DITHER: stored bytes equal the CPU model to within the rounding of the 8-bit conversion (no dithering noise); BLEND, DEPTH_TEST and CULL_FACE are also disabled for the sky and post-processing passes, which is not verified separately

visual_review.notes: 256x256 radeonsi es-max capture viewed at 3x (llvmpipe and zink captures differ from it in 36 isolated pixels, near sky contour steps and silhouettes; all six matrix captures are otherwise identical). Seven vertical stripes separated by one-pixel light lines, one continuous 3D picture behind them: checkerboard floor in perspective with warm and cool light pools, blue sphere with specular highlights, magenta cube, gold torus, teal cube, red spheres, dark purple sky with a glowing orange lamp. Stripe 1 raw: dark, high contrast. Stripes 2 and 3 gamma (shader / SRGB8_ALPHA8 scene): bright and alike. Stripe 4 blurred. Stripe 5 Sobel: white outlines of the torus, spheres, cube edges and floor grid on black. Stripe 6 bloom: glow around the lamp and on the bright floor. Stripe 7 depth of field: near cube and far floor soft, in-focus parts sharp. Single looks (keys 1-7) were also captured at 640x480 and checked: raw is dark, gamma matches the overview, the sRGB-scene look has about twice as many distinct sky colors (101 versus 48 in one column), Sobel is clean (no contour lines in the sky), bloom adds a soft halo, depth of field blurs the near magenta cube and the distant floor while the torus and the blue sphere stay sharp. Window-size review (claude-opus-5.5): gpu captures at 333x777 and 1000x200 viewed. The portrait surface keeps the square view's horizontal field of view, so the seven stripes show the same objects (blue sphere, magenta cube, gold torus, teal cube, red spheres and the orange lamp) with more sky above and more floor below; the 5:1 strip shows a wide view of the same scene.
